payload.goal: Add expense categories to the splitter. Extend the Expense type with an optional category field validated against a fixed set of categories, add computeCategoryTotals to the domain, expose listCategoryTotals from the API layer, render a category breakdown in the web surface, and cover the new behaviour with tests. Preserve the existing balance behaviour and keep the current tests green.

node.title: Expense categories
node.objective: Add optional validated expense categories, category totals, API exposure, web breakdown rendering, and regression coverage while preserving existing balance behavior.

node.title: Category domain model
node.objective: Extend the Expense domain model with an optional category field, centralize the fixed category set, validate category values, and cover valid, invalid, and missing category cases.

node.title: Category totals computation
node.objective: Add computeCategoryTotals to the domain without changing existing balance computation behavior, with tests for categorized and uncategorized expenses.

node.title: Category totals API
node.objective: Expose listCategoryTotals from the API layer using the domain computation and preserve existing API balance behavior.

node.title: Web category breakdown
node.objective: Render a category breakdown in the web summary surface using the API category totals while preserving the current balance summary.

breakdown.objective: The expense splitter supports optional validated categories, computes category totals, exposes them through the API layer, renders a web category breakdown, and keeps existing balance behavior and tests green.

acceptanceIntents.description: Expense accepts an optional category field validated against a fixed category set.
The domain exposes computeCategoryTotals for summing expenses by category.
The API layer exposes listCategoryTotals backed by the domain computation.
The web summary surface renders a category breakdown.
Existing balance behavior remains unchanged and current tests stay green.

root.title: Expense categories
root.objective: Add optional validated expense categories, category totals, API exposure, web breakdown rendering, and regression coverage while preserving existing balance behavior.
expectedOutcomes: Expenses may omit category or include one valid fixed category.
Invalid category values are rejected at the existing validation boundary.
Category totals are computed independently from balance totals.
The API exposes category totals for consumers.
The web summary displays category totals without removing existing balance output.
Existing balance tests remain valid.

complexitySignals.rationale: Touches the existing domain type, domain computation, API surface, web summary, and tests, but within four known files.

cut.rationale: Children are cut around cohesive behavior increments: category contract, total computation, API exposure, and web rendering. Each increment is independently verifiable while preserving the end-to-end category feature.

children.title: Category domain model
children.objective: Extend the Expense domain model with an optional category field, centralize the fixed category set, validate category values, and cover valid, invalid, and missing category cases.
expectedOutcomes: Expense includes an optional category field.
The accepted category values are represented in one fixed domain-owned set.
Missing category remains valid.
Invalid category values fail validation.
Existing expenses without category remain compatible.

complexitySignals.rationale: A narrow domain and test change, but it alters the exported Expense contract and validation behavior.

children.title: Category totals computation
children.objective: Add computeCategoryTotals to the domain without changing existing balance computation behavior, with tests for categorized and uncategorized expenses.
expectedOutcomes: computeCategoryTotals returns totals grouped by category.
Uncategorized expenses have defined handling in the computation.
Existing balance computation output remains unchanged for the same inputs.
Tests cover multiple categories and balance regression.

complexitySignals.rationale: Adds a domain export and focused tests while sharing context with existing expense calculations.

children.title: Category totals API
children.objective: Expose listCategoryTotals from the API layer using the domain computation and preserve existing API balance behavior.
expectedOutcomes: src/api/expenses.ts exports or otherwise exposes listCategoryTotals consistently with existing API style.
API category totals delegate to domain logic rather than duplicating computation.
API tests verify category totals and existing balance behavior.

complexitySignals.rationale: Introduces an API-facing function and must align with existing API patterns and domain contracts.

children.title: Web category breakdown
children.objective: Render a category breakdown in the web summary surface using the API category totals while preserving the current balance summary.
expectedOutcomes: src/web/summary.ts includes category breakdown output.
The existing balance summary remains visible and semantically unchanged.
Web tests or existing summary tests cover category breakdown rendering and no-category behavior.

complexitySignals.rationale: A focused web integration over existing API/domain behavior with rendering regression risk.

candidateArtifacts.purpose: Provide the authoritative fixed category set and Expense.category type used by domain computation, API exposure, and web rendering.

Expense.category is optional and restricted to the fixed category set owned by the domain module.

uncertainties.description: The supplied goal does not specify whether expenses without a category should be omitted from category totals or grouped under an uncategorized bucket.
uncertainties.impact: This changes observable computeCategoryTotals, API, and web output behavior.

uncertainties.description: The supplied goal requires validation against a fixed set of categories but does not enumerate the category names.
uncertainties.impact: The exact allowed values define validation behavior, tests, and user-facing labels.

questions.question: What fixed category values should be accepted for Expense.category?
questions.reason: The allowed values are part of the public domain contract and directly determine validation, tests, API output, and web labels.
options: Use product-specified values supplied by the human
Executor selects a small conventional set and documents it in tests

questions.question: Should expenses without category be omitted from category totals or grouped under an uncategorized bucket?
questions.reason: Expense.category is optional, so uncategorized handling affects domain totals, API output, and web rendering.
options: Omit uncategorized expenses from category totals
Group uncategorized expenses under an explicit Uncategorized bucket
